thesis: Iron ore is holding up better than feared - $100.02/t on 8 September, six-week highs on pre-holiday Chinese restocking - but the customer is sick underneath the price. Only about 30% of Chinese steelmakers were profitable as of 4 September, down from 61% a year ago, and BHP's own 63-day momentum has now turned negative. A firm spot price resting on restocking by loss-making mills is not something to add exposure against.
bull_case: The US$90/t downgrade trigger I worried about on 7 September has not arrived: iron ore rose to $100.02/t on 8 September and futures hit six-week highs around CNY 740/t on elevated freight costs and pre-holiday restocking. BHP kept FY2026 production guidance unchanged at 258-269Mt, so there is no operational problem. The FY2026 result on 18 August still stands - dividend raised to US$1.72, the highest in four years, net debt down to US$8.69B near the bottom of the target range - and copper remains the structural story. The position is +1.2% and the packet still shows close > SMA50 > SMA200 at A$63.44 native.
bear_case: The demand side is deteriorating in a way the spot price has not caught up with. Only ~30% of Chinese steelmakers were profitable as of 4 September, against 32.5% a week earlier and 61% a year ago; the blast-furnace operating rate has fallen to 89.08% with daily pig iron output declining. Mills that lose money on every tonne do not restock twice. Forecasters see iron ore averaging $95/t in 2026 with rising seaborne supply, persistent Chinese property weakness and elevated inventories all pointing lower. BHP is also in a pricing standoff with China's state-backed CMRG, part of a deliberate push to shift pricing power and settle contracts in yuan - a structural negative for the seller. Momentum has rolled over: 63d momentum -0.5%, score down to +0.34 from +0.40, RSI 49.
catalysts: Chinese steel mill profitability and blast-furnace rates after the holiday restock
29 Sep 2026 RBA decision and the AUD
risks: Only ~30% of Chinese steelmakers profitable, down from 61% a year ago
Iron ore forecast to average $95/t in 2026 against ~$100 spot
CMRG pricing standoff shifting pricing power to the buyer
63d momentum now negative at -0.5%; score falling
AUD strength on an RBA hike reducing translated earnings
invalidation: Flips long on a close above A$67.00 native with iron ore holding above $100/t and Chinese mill profitability recovering above 50%. The bear case confirms on iron ore closing below US$90/t for a week or a close below A$58.00 native, which breaks the SMA50.
